Vision and Values
Our school motto is: From little acorns mighty oaks do grow
At the heart of Oaklands Primary School are the values of respect for all, pride in ourselves and our school and the commitment to develop a love of learning. These values inspire everything that we do and ensure our children grow in to confident individuals with great aspirations for themselves, their futures and their communities. To do this we carefully nurture our pupils so that when they leave us they have excellent academic knowledge alongside the confidence, motivation and skills to apply themselves to any challenge.

pageCache.text:
Ealing Schools Counselling Partnership
The Space – A Place to Talk
We have a lunchtime drop-in every Thursday called The Space for children who feel vulnerable in the playground or who have something that is concerning them. This is a place where they can come and talk alone or with a friend about their worries. The service is provided by the Ealing Schools’ Counselling Partnership, funded by John Lyon, that we helped set up. If you do not want your child to use this service, please let us know.
Parents' Drop-In
As part of the Ealing Schools Counselling Partnership we offer a regular Parent’s Drop In at Oaklands, please contact William directly on 07368 857 699 our Therapeutic Lead if you would like to book an appointment. This is a strictly confidential space in which you may discuss any concerns you have about your child(ren) and/or receive emotional support due to difficulties that maybe going on in your life i.e. bereavement, separation, stress, anxiety, etc.
Please click here to view an updated leaflet in regards to Ealing Schools Counselling Partnership programme. They are always working to improve the emotional wellbeing of our children, parents and staff by working with the whole school community.

pageCache.text:
Wraparound Childcare - Rocket Club
At Oaklands, we offer a wraparound care club called The Rocket Club!
The Rocket Club is a way to support parents working full time to have affordable child-care in the safe environment of our school. It is a home from home for children who attend. The Rocket Breakfast Club runs from 7.45am - 8.50am and the Rocket After School Club from 3.20pm - 5.45pm or extended day to 6.15pm.
Cost per day
From September 2026, the cost per child per day is £6 for a breakfast club session, £15 for an afternoon session until 5.45pm and an additional £3 for an extended day option to stay until 6.15pm. For ad-hoc session please see below. Bookings are for Monday to Friday, Oaklands term time only. Fees will be reviewed annually
Ad-hoc Sessions
Please enquire at least a day in advance for any ad-hoc sessions (enquiry to rocket@oaklands.ealing.sch.uk), and once booked, it will not be possible to cancel an ad-hoc session. The cost for an afterschool ad-hoc session is £25. Payment will be required a day in advance (childcare vouchers and government scheme payment will not be accepted for ad-hoc bookings) and is non-refundable. For emergency same day requests please call finance. In order to organise staffing, payment must be received through Scopay by midday. If you have not paid by midday we will not be able to accept the booking, and you should collect your child after school, and again childcare vouchers will not be accepted for ad hoc.
Ms Ash is our Manager and Mrs Gamea our Deputy Manager. Ms Temple is the Finance Administrator for Rocket Club.
To apply for a place at Rocket Club please click on the link below and complete the form. Please note places will be offered as per the terms and conditions. If we cannot offer a place initially, you will be kept on a waiting list. If you apply after the deadline which is Monday 1st June 2026, midday you will be offered a place if any are available, or you will be added to the waiting list.
For queries please email rocket@oaklands.ealing.sch.uk
Please click here to view the terms and conditions.

School Meals at Oaklands Primary School
Hello from your new caterers
ISS 'Feeding Hungry Minds' will provide food services at your child's school from September. Our philosophy is to serve tasty, fresh, healthy and sustainably sourced food that you can trust.
We are members of the Ealing Healthy Schools' Project and encourage all children to eat a balanced diet.
We recognise that a balanced and varied diet is essential for maintaining both physical and mental health in children. ISS nutritionists team check every menu to make sure that they offer a variety of different foods to help pupils thrive throughout the school day.
For further information you can contact telephone ISS on 01924 792 334 or alternatively 01483 516 703
The support teams are available from 9am to 4pm, Monday to Friday.
Guide to school lunches
How to register my child's school meal account

Please note that even though the children in Reception to Year 2 receive universal free school meals, you still need to register your children's details with ISS.

All children in Reception, Y1 and Y2 are entitled to universal free school meals via the government initiative.
The Major of London announced a new initiative to receive free school meals this academic year for KS2. All meals are free and you will not be invoiced by ISS, please take full advantage of this scheme! Once again you will still need to register your child's details with ISS.

If you would prefer for your child to bring a packed lunch from home, please ensure that ISS are aware of this so that you are not incorrectly charged for meals. It is important that packed lunches provide as healthy and balanced lunch as what they would eat at home.

School Meal Debt - Only applies to Nursery
Whilst the majority of families keep their school meal accounts topped up, some parents do persistently run up debt. Where these debts occur, the school is charged. This means that money which should be spent on our children’s education is instead used to cover outstanding debts.
We operate a one-week credit limit of £11.75. If an account exceeds this limit, your child will not be provided with a school meal and you must instead provide a packed lunch.
In these circumstances, parents will initially be sent a text message advising them of this.
We would like to remind parents that it is their responsibility to ensure that their child has food at lunchtime, not the school’s. Please ensure your school meal account is kept in credit.
Payments can be made once you have registered via your account either using debit/credit cards or calling our catering company (ISS) at their local Ealing Office, 020 3903 0412.

Educational Trips, Visits and Extra Curricular Opportunities at Oaklands
At Oaklands Primary School, we are committed to enriching our students' educational experiences through a diverse range of trips, visits, and extra-curricular activities.
Educational Trips and Visits
We believe that interactive, real-world experiences significantly enhance learning. To bring our curriculum to life, we organise various trips and visits that provide hands-on learning opportunities. For instance, our students have explored historical landmarks to deepen their understanding of history, visited science museums to engage with practical scientific concepts, and attended theatre productions to appreciate literature and the arts. These experiences not only reinforce classroom learning but also help students connect their studies to the world around them.
We feel that children should learn as interactively as possible so that they can relate their experiences to the real world. Each subject area ensures that children have experience of “hands on” practical tasks and there are also trips and visits arranged that augment our curriculum topics to ensure they come alive.
Upcoming Trips and Visits
We are pleased to inform you about our forthcoming educational trips and visits. These experiences are designed to enrich our curriculum and provide students with hands-on learning opportunities that connect classroom lessons to the real world.
Watch this space! Our trips and visits schedule is currently being finalised, and we will be updating this page shortly with all the details.
Extra Curricular Clubs - Before and After School Clubs
In addition to educational trips, we offer a wide variety of before and after school clubs designed to cater to our pupils' diverse interests and talents. These clubs provide opportunities to enhance specific areas of the curriculum and develop new skills. We try to ensure that every child is guaranteed the opportunity to participate in at least one club per term. Each term, we publish a newsletter detailing the available clubs, and parents can sign up for those they wish to attend. We strive to allocate club placements as fairly as possible to ensure all pupils have the chance to engage in activities they are passionate about.
For more information about our extra-curricular clubs or to access this term's clubs newsletter, please contact Ms. Packham. We are dedicated to providing our pupils with a well-rounded education that extends beyond the classroom, fostering a love for learning and personal growth.
Extra-Curricular Clubs Newsletter
Our extra-curricular clubs for the new academic year are currently being finalised. We are looking forward to another exciting year of activities and opportunities for our students to learn new skills, explore their interests and try something new.

We also encourage you to visit our Community Learning Hub page for details about our community supplementary schools, which offer additional learning opportunities and resources for our students and their families. ​

French
Oaklands focus - to experience the joy of learning about people from another culture and to develop the skills and knowledge to understand and communicate with them.
French is taught by specialist teacher and native speaker. Ms Osmani is a French national and was a secondary school AST. She has worked to develop her own curriculum overview and lesson plans following the school SOLO plans. Her lessons are interactive and focus on developing confidence and enthusiasm for speaking and communicating in French. This is followed by a development of these skills into reading and writing. We use similar techniques as Read, Write Inc to support the children’s development of reading and writing skills. Each unit has a final product that the children need to achieve and a final “mastery” task that is used to support teacher assessment against the learning objectives of the unit.

Governors
Governing Body Structure
Each governor is a member of the Full Governing Board. The Board operates under a flat structure in which there are no committees, but each governor takes on two areas of responsibility.
Meet the Governors
Who's Who
Mr Darryl Evans - Chair of Governing Body
Term of Office - 9 September 2019 - 8 September 2027
Mr Evans is the Chair of the Governing Body. He was co-opted as a governor in 2019 having had no prior connection to the school. He is also a governor of Barnes Primary School in the London Borough of Richmond-upon-Thames. He is a retired solicitor who ran his own legal practice, specialising in employment law, and prior to that was a partner at PricewaterhouseCoopers Legal. He now only works voluntarily, in the education and prison sectors.
Mr William Blanchard - Co-Vice-Chair of Governors, Co-opted Governor
Term of Office -9 September 2019 - 8 September 2027
Mr Blanchard works within the education sector, providing compliance and legal advice to both primary and secondary schools, predominantly relating to data protection and privacy. It is as a result of this that he first became involved with Oaklands Primary School. Previously he worked in asylum and human rights law in Gray’s Inn, on the Hillsborough Inquest and for the Treasury Solicitor.
Mr Edward Rowley - Co-Vice-Chair of Governors and Parent Governor
Term of Office - 14/12/2022 - 13/12/2026
Mr Rowley is a parent governor and has lived locally since childhood and in Hanwell since 2009. Mr Rowley is a senior manager at Transport for London and manages London Underground’s Tube Trains, he has a range of experience including engineering, finance and HR as well as health and safety and estate / asset management. Mr Rowley has two children at Oaklands.
Ms Tzaddi Allick-Hamilton - Co-opted Governor
Term of Office -18 December 2023 - 17 December 2027
Ms Allick-Hamilton has a long background in Arts, Wellbeing and Education, having trained in creative fields with a focus on Theatre and Music, including at the Harvard Graduate School of Education. She holds a professional mini MBA from SOAS University of London. She has worked and taught in London, New York and Paris. Today, she is an active member of the borough of Ealing where she was raised, running her business at the same time as being a parent, a governor and a member of the Caribbean and African Collective Ealing and actively supporting various initiatives to improve maternal health outcomes and wellbeing equity.
Ms Ros Brooks - Staff Governor
Term of Office -15 January 2024 - 14 January 2028
Ms Brooks has been a teacher for 20 years and has been at Oaklands Primary School since 2016. She is currently the EYFS phase leader and also leads the school's work on oracy. She is a member of the school's PSA. Ms Brooks has a passion for providing early years education and inspiring a love of learning in everything the school does.
Mr Nicholas Clark – Parent Governor
Term of Office – 25 March 2024 – 24 March 2028

Maths
Oaklands Focus – to have a deep understanding of mathematical concepts and the confidence and skills to enjoy solving problems in a range of contexts.
We use careful formative assessment and the White Rose hub materials to support teachers to create plans which are carefully designed to meet children’s needs. We apply the principles of Mastery to ensure all learners have deep understanding which allows them to apply their learning in a range of familiar and unfamiliar contexts. Children are supported to develop that understanding by using a range of teaching strategies including emphasis on using models and representations to illustrate thinking, structures to support vocabulary and sentence building to help explain reasoning and opportunities to apply their learning to problem solving activities.
The teaching programme prioritises children’s learning about number in the autumn term and spends a lot of time securing their understanding which is then revisited as part of other topics throughout the rest of the year.
Mathematics is also taught through other curriculum areas. For example, experiences to use measures in real life contexts are incorporated in to the science and DT (Food Tech) curriculums, opportunities to gather and manipulate statistics are developed in geography.
Mathematics is also supported through home learning and online learning using TT Rockstars and Numbots to secure automaticity in recalling number facts and MyMaths to practise the wider maths curriculum.

Music
Oaklands focus – to have the knowledge and confidence to celebrate themselves and the world through listening to and making music.
Children and teachers engage enthusiastically in music and recognise that it as a way of bringing the whole community together. Over time, children develop their repertoire of traditional and contemporary songs from a range of cultures and understand how to control their breathing and posture. They develop knowledge of the different musical elements and structures and recognise how different choices create different effects, both in their roles as composers and listeners. They experience playing a range of tuned and un-tuned instruments and experience composing and recording their ideas in different ways. They learn about the history of music and value different musical traditions from across the world.
Musical learning is developed in two ways. The formal curriculum provides a series of learning journeys which are effectively designed to build on prior understanding and work towards a defined end point. They are based on the latest understanding of cognition to ensure children learn as effectively as possible. These discrete lessons are taught by both musical specialists and non-specialist teachers and curriculum planning recognises the range of subject knowledge and skills different teachers bring to the subject. The informal curriculum provides a broad range of experiences and musical opportunities and builds links between different subjects (musical tables songs, songs to support learning in other subjects like history and PSHE, moving and dancing to music in PE etc). Weekly singing assemblies provide opportunities to build the children’s repertoire of songs and skills and understand how ensembles work. Knowledge of musical elements, structures and traditions are reinforced and revisited regularly through assembly to help embed deep learning. Performances such as Christmas plays and End of Key Stage graduations provide opportunities to hone performance skills and reinforces the importance of music in the life of the school. Extra-curricular activities such as Recorder/Ukulele club and peripatetic music lessons also provide children with opportunities to develop their learning.
The impact of teaching music is evident across the school. Children often choose to sing at playtimes and singing and music can be heard across the school throughout the day. Whole-school and parental engagement is improved through performances which are well attended. Participation in music develops wellbeing, promotes listening and develops concentration. It supports cohesion across the community and supports the school provision of SMSC. We want to ensure that music is enjoyed by teachers and pupils across school and encourage them to build a life-long love of learning in music. Teachers make formal assessments of children’s progress and attainment in music as part of the annual report to parents.

pageCache.text:
Admissions
How do I get a place at Oaklands?
We accommodate children from ages 3-11. We strongly recommend families come and visit us first. We do a Parent Tour every TUESDAY from 9.00am - 10.30am, usually with the Headteacher. We advise all parents to tour a school before reading reports etc. You will know if the school feels right for your family!
Helping Your Child Start School with Confidence
Starting school is an important milestone, and we are committed to supporting families to ensure a smooth and positive transition into Reception.
The government has published helpful guidance for parents and carers, offering practical advice on how to prepare children for starting school. You can read this here:
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/getting-children-ready-for-reception-supporting-effective-transition/supporting-a-smooth-transition-into-reception
We also recommend this fun and engaging video by MC Grammar, which shares simple tips to help children feel confident and ready for school: Watch here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yfSNhFiVgT8&list=RDyfSNhFiVgT8&start_radio=1
These resources provide useful ideas to help children develop independence, confidence, and key skills ahead of starting Nursery and Reception.
Applying for a place in our Nursery
As a school we can only deal directly with parents for Nursery admissions. The application form is below. Once your child is 3 years old we can take them in our Nursery if there are spaces, but you can put your application in after your child turns 2.
If there is a waiting list the priority criteria used is: Criteria 1 Looked After Child, Child In Need, SEN child
Criteria 2 Sibling who will be at Oaklands in September of the following academic year
Criteria 3 No sibling
Spaces are then allocated on the distance from child's home address to the school (in a straight line) determined by Ealing Borough.
A sibling link is defined as the prospective Nursery child having a brother or sister (including step brothers and sisters or LAC siblings) on roll at Oaklands at the same time that they would start.
Please contact the School Office as we still have a few remaining spaces.
Please click here to download a Nursery Registration Form
Complete the above Registration form and return to the School Office to register your interest at Oaklands Nursery. Please note a place at our Nursery does not guarantee a place in our Reception.
Reception Admissions
All Reception places are allocated by Ealing Council's admission criteria. For more information please visit the relevant section of their website, we have added a link below.
In-Year Admissions
Ealing Council makes decisions for admission to Oaklands Primary School for pupils entering Y1 to Year 6, in-line with all local maintained community Primary schools. Prospective parents should contact Ealing Council to find out about admission arrangement and to enquire about waiting lists.
They will also guide you on school availability and next steps.
If you are offered a place by Ealing Council, they will inform us and then you can contact us to finalise induction.
Once you have a accepted offer for an in-year admissions place at Oaklands, contact Miss McCarthy on 0208 567 5243. Miss McCarthy will arrange a pre-admission meeting to complete relevant paperwork.
If at any time you have a query about admissions, speak to Miss McCarthy or any of the Office team!
For more information about Reception or In-Year Admissions, please visit the Ealing Council Schools’ Admissions Page
